gates.notes: A tenant-scoped findFirst (where id AND tenantId = ctx.user.tenantId, select id only) now runs before assertAppointmentWithinAvailability and before the use case. An unknown, malformed or foreign id throws NOT_FOUND with no availability, settings or closure read, so no availability answer about someone else's booking. The test asserts the where clause, that appointmentSettings.findUnique and the use case are not called. Zod input validation still runs first, as before.

gates.gate: enumeration / information disclosure of the NOT_FOUND
gates.notes: Message is 'Appointment with ID <id> not found' and only echoes the id the caller sent. Unknown and foreign ids produce the identical code and message, so existence in another tenant is not distinguishable. Nothing from the target row is read beyond id. Same wording as the other NOT_FOUNDs in this router. The extra lookup adds one indexed query and does not create a timing difference between unknown and foreign ids (both are a null result from the same query).

The use case still does its own forTenant(tenantId).findById and returns ValidationError 'Appointment not found: <id>' (mapped via mapDomainErrorToTRPC). It is now reachable only in a delete race between the router lookup and the use case read, or for ids the router lookup accepts but the AppointmentId value object rejects; the message is equally non-leaky (own input id) and tenant scoped, but the tRPC code on that path differs from the router's NOT_FOUND. Cosmetic, no security effect. Behaviour change worth noting: a malformed id previously returned a validation error and now returns NOT_FOUND.

startMinute BETWEEN 0 AND 1439 and endMinute BETWEEN 1 AND 1440, renamed to *_bounds_check; now exactly matches the Zod bounds. Strictly tighter, additive table, no existing rows. Migration is merged-not-applied, so editing it in place does not break a checksum on any applied environment (assumes none applied, per migration header; not verified against a database). RLS, FKs and the rest unchanged. SQL re-review APPROVE per lead (not re-read).

Renders a static message ('will be available after the next release') for NOT_FOUND on the get query. No server text rendered, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Invalidate failures are now logged with the error object via console.error (no user data). Note: any NOT_FOUND from get shows this notice; the get procedure has no other NOT_FOUND path.
